body.heading: The green fades away
paragraphs: In spring and summer, leaves are busy making food from sunlight. The green colour in leaves, called chlorophyll, helps them do this job.
When days get shorter and colder, the tree stops making food. The green colour slowly fades, like a drawing left in the sun.

body.heading: Colours that were hiding
paragraphs: Yellow and orange colours were inside the leaf all along. You could not see them because the strong green covered them up.
Red and purple colours are different. Some trees make them fresh in autumn to protect the leaf while the tree takes back useful food for winter.

body.heading: The tree is resting, not dying
paragraphs: When the leaves fall, the tree is getting ready to rest through winter. Under the ground, its roots stay alive and busy.
In spring, the tree will grow brand-new leaves and start making food again. The fallen leaves feed the soil and tiny creatures all winter long.
